meta.actor: Claude — consolidation pass (no research, no content rewriting)
meta.scope: Every Grok batch file for Guyana merged into one file. Records are byte-faithful to the batches except for the normalisations listed in _consolidation.

reports.title: Bureau of Statistics (BoS) — institutional statistical identity
reports.description: National statistical office. Produces census, labour-force, national-accounts and other official statistics.
reports._notes: Institutional parent node for Guyanese official statistics. Semi-autonomous body under the Minister of Finance.
_referenced_by: Budget and planning documents that cite BoS series

reports.title: Population and Housing Census
reports.description: Decennial population and housing census. 2022 census recorded 878,674 persons (up 17.6% from 2012), reversing prior decline; projections approach ~950k+ by mid-decade.
reports._notes: Foundational demographic product. Documents the demographic turnaround coincident with the oil boom and rising foreign-born share.

reports.title: Labour Force Survey
reports.description: Periodic household labour-force survey producing participation, employment and unemployment rates. Recent rounds show improving indicators but large gender gaps.
reports._notes: Core labour-market product. Male participation and employment substantially exceed female rates; women’s unemployment is roughly double men’s in recent readings.

reports.title: Bank of Guyana — statistical publications
reports.description: Central-bank statistical output covering monetary aggregates, external accounts, inflation and related macroeconomic series.
reports._notes: Monetary and external statistical authority. Complements BoS on prices, balance of payments and financial-sector indicators.

reports.title: Natural Resource Fund (NRF)
reports.publisher: Government of Guyana / Ministry of Finance
reports.description: Sovereign wealth fund that receives and manages oil revenues under the Natural Resource Fund Act. Central fiscal institution of the oil era; balance reached multi-billion USD levels; withdrawal rules amended to accelerate public investment.
reports._notes: Core fiscal-governance node of the oil boom. Continuously cited in budget, sustainability and intergenerational-equity analysis. Withdrawals now finance a large share of public investment and current spending.
reports._url_evidence: Ministry of Finance publications section for the Natural Resource Fund; page lists the NRF Act 2019/2021, the Operational Agreement and the NRF monthly and quarterly reports.

reports.title: Oil production (Stabroek / Liza and subsequent FPSOs)
reports.description: Offshore crude-oil production from the Stabroek Block and subsequent developments. Production has risen from zero (pre-2019) to the high-hundreds of thousands of barrels per day, driving extreme GDP growth.
reports._notes: Transformative production node. Output growth is the direct driver of the multi-year double-digit real GDP expansion and of NRF inflows. Continuously cited as the structural break in Guyana’s economic history.
reports._url_evidence: Data Centre of the Ministry of Natural Resources' Petroleum Management Programme; lists official oil production, oil price, gas produced/flared and per-field production data series.

reports.title: Production Sharing Agreement — ExxonMobil consortium
reports.publisher: Government of Guyana / ExxonMobil / Hess / CNOOC
reports.description: Production-sharing agreement governing the Stabroek Block and related developments. Defines royalty (2% on gross production) and profit-oil split that feed the Natural Resource Fund.
reports._notes: Foundational commercial and fiscal contract. Continuously cited as the legal and fiscal framework that converts physical production into government revenue.
reports._url_evidence: Official Petroleum Management Programme document page providing the Stabroek Block Petroleum (production sharing) Agreement dated 7 October 2016.

reports.title: National Accounts / GDP
reports.publisher: Bureau of Statistics / Bank of Guyana
reports.description: System of national accounts producing GDP by production and expenditure. Extreme oil-driven growth has lifted nominal GDP into the mid-to-high tens of billions of USD and per-capita GDP into upper-middle / near high-income territory on paper.
reports._notes: Core macroeconomic product. Growth rates in the mid-to-high teens (and higher in peak years) are almost entirely oil-driven; non-oil GDP grows more moderately and is itself partly stimulated by oil-financed public spending.

reports.title: Georgetown / Region Four (Demerara-Mahaica)
reports.description: Capital city and the most populous administrative region. Primary urban and commercial domain; absorbs a large share of construction and service activity linked to the oil boom.
reports._notes: Lived urban core of the transformation. Census and construction indicators show rapid housing and building growth concentrated here.

reports.title: Poverty measurement (historical and residual)
reports.publisher: Bureau of Statistics / World Bank / independent
reports.description: Poverty headcount and related indicators. Pre-oil poverty was among the highest in South America; recent official poverty series are sparse, limiting assessment of how the boom has translated into broad-based welfare gains.
reports._notes: Critical social-gap node. Pre-oil poverty headcount was very high (~40%+ in older readings). Lack of recent comprehensive poverty data is a recognised constraint on evaluating the inclusiveness of the oil-driven expansion.

reports.title: FPSO fleet (Liza Destiny, Liza Unity, Prosperity, ONE Guyana)
reports.description: Floating Production, Storage and Offloading vessels that constitute current production capacity. Four vessels online; further FPSOs (Uaru/Errea Wittu and beyond) scheduled to push capacity toward 1.3 mbd.
reports._notes: Physical production platform. Each successive FPSO has driven step-changes in output and in NRF inflows. Continuously cited in production and revenue tracking.
reports._url_evidence: Official petroleum ministry data chart of production by the Liza, Unity Gold and Payara Gold streams (the Destiny/Unity/Prosperity FPSOs) from 20 Dec 2019 to 30 Jun 2026; no official page exists for the 'FPSO fleet' as such, and ONE Guyana is not yet broken out.

reports.title: NRF inflows and withdrawals
reports.publisher: Bank of Guyana / Ministry of Finance
reports.description: Periodic reporting of deposits into and withdrawals from the Natural Resource Fund (profit oil, royalties, signature bonuses; approved budget transfers).
reports._notes: Operational fiscal pulse of the oil era. Cumulative deposits multi-billion USD; withdrawals finance a large and rising share of the national budget. Balance tracked in the low-to-mid single-digit billions of USD.

reports.title: Non-oil GDP
reports.publisher: Bureau of Statistics / Bank of Guyana
reports.description: GDP excluding crude-oil extraction. Grows more moderately than headline GDP but is itself stimulated by oil-financed public investment and local-content activity.
reports._notes: Key analytical distinction. Non-oil growth in the high-single to low-double digits is frequently cited as evidence of spillovers; critics note that much of it is still oil-money circulating through construction and public services.

reports.title: National Budget
reports.description: Annual national budget. Increasingly financed by NRF withdrawals; supports large public investment, cash transfers, wages and social programmes.
reports._notes: Operational spending framework of the boom. NRF transfers now cover a material share (order of 30%+) of a rapidly expanding budget.
reports._url_evidence: Ministry of Finance budget landing page listing the annual Budget Speech, Budget At A Glance and Budget Estimates volumes for 2026, 2025 and earlier years.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index / Inflation
reports.publisher: Bureau of Statistics / Bank of Guyana
reports.description: Urban consumer price index and inflation measures. Inflation has remained relatively contained compared with regional peers, with food prices the main driver.
reports._notes: Price-stability node. Average inflation in the low-to-mid single digits in recent years; food inflation higher and more relevant for poorer households.

reports.title: Balance of Payments / External accounts
reports.description: Balance of payments and external-sector statistics. Large current-account surpluses driven by oil exports; capital account reflects FPSO and related investment imports.
reports._notes: External counterpart of the oil boom. Current-account surplus remains large even as import bills for FPSOs and investment goods spike in delivery years.

reports.title: Local Content Act / local-content regime
reports.description: Legal and regulatory framework requiring and monitoring local participation in the oil and gas value chain. Intended channel for non-oil employment and enterprise development.
reports._notes: Spillover-policy node. Continuously cited as the main institutional attempt to convert oil activity into broader domestic employment and firm growth.
reports._url_evidence: Official Local Content Register of the Ministry of Natural Resources / Local Content Secretariat, hosting the full text of the Local Content Act 2021.

reports.title: Cash transfers and social grants
reports.description: Expanding set of cash grants, vouchers and social transfers financed in part by NRF withdrawals. Visible instrument of oil-revenue redistribution.
reports._notes: Lived redistribution node. Budget documents and independent commentary track the growth of cash grants and related transfers as a primary way households feel the oil boom.
reports._url_evidence: Government of Guyana official cash grant portal (coat of arms, 'Powered by OPM NDMA') for registration, identity verification and bank payment of the $100,000 cash grant.

reports.title: Public debt
reports.publisher: Ministry of Finance / Bank of Guyana
reports.description: Stock of public debt relative to GDP. Remains moderate by regional standards despite rapid spending growth, supported by oil-revenue inflows.
reports._notes: Sustainability indicator. Debt-to-GDP has risen modestly with domestic issuance but stays well below levels typical of stressed regional peers.
reports._url_evidence: Ministry of Finance Public Debt Reports section listing the Public Debt Annual Report series (2015-2018, 2020).

reports.title: CARICOM membership
reports.description: Membership of the Caribbean Community. Primary regional-integration framework for trade, movement and political coordination.
reports._notes: Core regional-architecture node. Continuously cited as Guyana’s principal formal integration framework in the Caribbean.
reports._url_evidence: CARICOM Secretariat's official country profile for Guyana, stating 'Date of Membership in CARICOM: 1 Aug 1973' and Guyana's quasi-Cabinet responsibility for agriculture and food security.

reports.title: Region 4 (Demerara-Mahaica) — coastal demographic core
reports.description: Most populous administrative region (~40% of national population). Contains Georgetown and the densest coastal settlement.
reports._notes: Demographic and economic core. Continuously cited as the primary concentration of population, formal activity and oil-boom construction.

reports.title: Hinterland regions (1, 7, 8, 9)
reports.publisher: Bureau of Statistics / Ministry of Amerindian Affairs
reports.description: Interior regions that hold the large majority of national land area but a small share of population. Highest Indigenous population shares and historically highest poverty rates.
reports._notes: Structural geographic contrast. ~12–13% of population on two-thirds of the land; poverty and service gaps have historically been several times higher than on the coast.

reports.title: Amerindian / Indigenous population and villages
reports.publisher: Bureau of Statistics / Ministry of Amerindian Affairs
reports.description: Indigenous (Amerindian) population statistics and the system of titled and untitled villages. Fourth-largest ethnic group nationally; majority population in hinterland regions 1, 8 and 9.
reports._notes: Core identity and territorial node. Continuously cited in land-rights, poverty and service-delivery analysis; titled Amerindian lands cover a material share of national territory.

reports.title: Education system — coverage, grants and feeding
reports.description: Education-sector statistics and programmes: school infrastructure, Because We Care cash grant, uniform grant, school-feeding programme, and exam-fee support. Large and rising budget allocation financed in part by oil revenues.
reports._notes: Primary human-capital and redistribution channel. Because We Care and school feeding are the most visible household-level education supports; hinterland and riverain schools receive targeted hot-meal and infrastructure attention.

reports.title: Because We Care cash grant
reports.publisher: Ministry of Education / Government of Guyana
reports.description: Per-child cash grant paid to families of schoolchildren (public and private). Flagship education-linked transfer expanded under the oil-revenue budget.
reports._notes: Lived cash-transfer node. Continuously cited as the main direct financial support reaching most school-age children; amount has been raised in successive budgets.
reports._url_evidence: Ministry of Education landing page for the 'Because We Care' government cash grant, describing the per-child grant, uniform voucher and grant increases.

reports.title: National School Feeding Programme
reports.description: School-meal programme providing breakfast and hot meals, with particular emphasis on hinterland and riverain schools.
reports._notes: Complementary in-kind support. Explicitly prioritises hinterland attendance and nutrition; also creates local catering livelihoods.
reports._url_evidence: Ministry of Education department page describing the National School Feeding Programme: targets all nursery and Grade 1-2 primary schools, regions covered, with Regions 7, 8 and 9 targeted separately; no dedicated programme landing page exists.

reports.title: Health system — access and hinterland gaps
reports.publisher: Ministry of Health / Bureau of Statistics
reports.description: Public health-system statistics and outcomes. National indicators have improved but remain below regional averages; access and quality gaps are largest in the hinterland.
reports._notes: Human-capital counterpart to education. Continuously cited for interior service-delivery challenges and for the need to convert oil revenues into better health outcomes outside the coastal strip.
reports._url_evidence: Bureau of Statistics data table 'Number of Health Institutions by Type and by Region, Guyana: 2024' (391 facilities across the 10 regions), sourced from the Ministry of Health statistical unit.

reports.title: Gold production and exports
reports.publisher: Guyana Gold Board / Bureau of Statistics
reports.description: Gold production and export statistics. Long-standing non-oil extractive sector, important in hinterland livelihoods and as a residual export earner.
reports._notes: Primary non-oil extractive node. Continues to matter for hinterland employment and for export diversification even as oil dominates the aggregate accounts.
reports._url_evidence: Guyana Gold Board documents repository listing Annual Reports (2013-2022), financial statements, Gold Exports 2020-2023 and GGB & Dealer Declarations 2020-2023.

reports.title: Rice and sugar — traditional agriculture
reports.publisher: Bureau of Statistics / Guyana Sugar Corporation / GRDB
reports.description: Rice and sugar production and export statistics. Historic coastal agricultural pillars that remain relevant for employment and rural livelihoods even as their relative economic weight has declined.
reports._notes: Traditional coastal agro-export nodes. Continuously cited in non-oil sector analysis and in discussions of rural employment outside the oil and construction boom.

reports.title: Bauxite production
reports.description: Bauxite production and export statistics. Historic extractive sector, mainly in Region 10 and related areas; residual non-oil industrial activity.
reports._notes: Legacy industrial-extractive node. Completes the non-oil primary-sector set alongside gold, rice and sugar.

reports.title: Guyana Power and Light (GPL)
reports.description: State-owned vertically integrated electricity utility. Serves the large majority of grid-connected customers; peak demand has roughly doubled with the oil-driven construction and commercial boom.
reports._notes: Core power-system node. Customer base and peak demand have risen sharply (peak demand from ~120 MW in 2020 toward 200+ MW); capacity additions and the forthcoming gas-to-energy project are the main responses.
reports._url_evidence: Guyana Power and Light Inc.'s own site, Publications > Annual Reports listing (2009-2012); the item is a utility rather than a publication, so this is its official report series page.

reports.title: Gas-to-Energy project (Wales)
reports.description: Associated-gas pipeline and combined-cycle power plant project intended to bring offshore gas ashore for domestic power generation and to lower electricity costs.
reports._notes: Strategic energy-transition node. Continuously cited as the main near-term solution to high-cost, fuel-oil-based generation and as a link between the oil sector and domestic industrial potential.
reports._url_evidence: Gas to Energy section of the Ministry of Natural Resources' Petroleum Management Programme, carrying the Public Notice of GTE Project Approval and links to GTE project documents.

reports.title: Housing programme / housing development
reports.publisher: Ministry of Housing / Government of Guyana
reports.description: Large-scale public housing and house-lot allocation programme. One of the most visible uses of oil-financed public investment on the coast.
reports._notes: Lived boom indicator. Budget allocations for housing are among the largest functional lines; new schemes and construction are transforming the coastal landscape around Georgetown and secondary towns.
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved and read: the Central Housing and Planning Authority's Home Construction Assistance Programme page, which sets out the programme's actual terms - three house types with government-set prices (two-bedroom flat house G$7,000,000; three-bedroom flat bungalow G$9,000,000; three-bedroom elevated house G$12,000,000) plus eligibility, household-income and land-tenure documentation requirements. This is a substantive programme page, not a homepage. The slug found in the first pass (/home-construction-assistance-programme/ and /home-subsidy-programme/) is a stub or 404; the '-2' variant is the live page.

reports.title: Roads, bridges and transport infrastructure
reports.description: National programme of road, bridge and corridor investment (coastal highways, Linden–Lethem, hinterland roads, river transport). Major oil-financed capital expenditure.
reports._notes: Physical integration node. Continuously cited as the attempt to link hinterland and coastal markets and to support the construction and logistics boom.
reports._url_evidence: Ministry of Public Works projects page listing current road, bridge and port works (Soesdyke-Linden Highway, East Bank Public Road, Mackenzie-Wismar Bridge, Parika port).

reports.title: Public investment programme
reports.description: Overall public capital expenditure financed increasingly by NRF withdrawals. Encompasses energy, transport, housing, health and education infrastructure.
reports._notes: Aggregate fiscal-impulse node. Budget size has multiplied since the start of oil production; capital spending is the primary channel through which oil revenue enters the domestic economy.
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved and read: Guyana Ministry of Finance Mid-Year Report 2025, which reports the Public Sector Investment Programme explicitly - 'At the end of the first half of this year, PSIP expenditure totalled $247 billion, 51.6 percent higher when compared with the same period in 2024', with the domestic portfolio at $215 billion, $7.6 billion of foreign-funded projects, and the full-year PSIP revised up to $784.2 billion from $737.7 billion. This is the Ministry's recurring PSIP reporting product, listed at https://finance.gov.gy/mid-year-reports/.

reports.title: EITI / extractive-sector transparency
reports.description: Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative reporting and related disclosure of oil, gas and mining revenues and payments.
reports._notes: Governance counterpart to the NRF. Continuously cited in discussions of revenue transparency and accountability in the oil era.
reports._url_evidence: GYEITI's official site, Country Report archive listing the seven Guyana EITI country reports from FY2017 through FY2023.

reports.title: Foreign direct investment statistics
reports.publisher: Bank of Guyana / Bureau of Statistics
reports.description: FDI flows and stocks. Dominated by oil-sector investment (ExxonMobil consortium and related service companies); non-oil FDI is smaller but rising with construction and services.
reports._notes: External-investment counterpart of the production boom. Continuously cited in balance-of-payments and growth analysis.

reports.title: Region 10 (Upper Demerara-Berbice) — Linden industrial/mining
reports.description: Interior region centred on Linden. Historic bauxite and industrial centre; gateway corridor toward the deeper hinterland (Linden–Lethem).
reports._notes: Secondary industrial and transport node. Completes the set of major regions beyond the pure coastal core and the deep hinterland.

reports.title: Water and sanitation access
reports.publisher: Guyana Water Inc. / Bureau of Statistics
reports.description: Household access to improved water and sanitation. Coastal coverage is higher; hinterland and riverain gaps remain material.
reports._notes: Basic-services node. Continuously cited alongside electricity as a constraint on living standards outside the best-served coastal areas.
reports._url_evidence: Retrieved and read: Guyana Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey 2019-2020, Survey Findings Report (Government of Guyana and UNICEF), published in the Bureau of Statistics publications catalogue. Chapter 10 ('Live in a safe and clean environment') carries the water and sanitation access statistics - drinking-water source and service level, sanitation facilities and handwashing - with tables disaggregated by region and population group. This is the official household-survey source for water and sanitation coverage; Guyana Water Inc. publishes only service descriptions and water-quality tests.

reports.title: Amaila Falls hydropower (project)
reports.description: Long-planned large hydropower project in the interior. Intended long-run renewable complement to gas-to-energy and thermal generation.
reports._notes: Long-horizon energy node. Continuously cited as the major renewable option for eventual surplus power and industrialisation; implementation has faced repeated delays.
reports._url_evidence: Guyana Energy Agency hydropower page describing the Amaila Falls project (developer, licences, completed feasibility study and EIA, ~103 MW run-of-river scheme); it is a project rather than a publication and the page content is dated.

dependencies.basis: Production volumes and fiscal take are governed by the Production Sharing Agreement.
NRF inflows are the fiscal expression of the royalty and profit-oil terms of the PSA.
Oil value-added dominates recent GDP growth.
Approved NRF withdrawals are a major financing source of the national budget.
Cash grants and social transfers are increasingly financed by NRF withdrawals.
NRF withdrawals are the primary financing source of the expanded public investment programme.

_consolidation.json_syntax_repair_note: These batch files were not valid JSON as delivered: "releases_per_year" carried an unquoted text value (missing opening quote), e.g. `"releases_per_year": continuous",`. Repaired mechanically by re-quoting the value verbatim. No number was invented.
_consolidation.cadence_note: A non-numeric cadence text was moved off releases_per_year into _cadence_original verbatim and the numeric field omitted, per the v2 spec (omitted, never null). Needs a human/judgement pass to become a real number.

_normalisation.note: Second pass, 2026-08-18: mechanical alignment to src/lib/types.ts. Nothing researched, nothing invented. Every original value that was replaced is preserved on the record under a key prefixed with an underscore.
rules: jurisdiction_level mapped into the six-value union; the delivered string kept as _jurisdiction_level_original.
domains: format-normalised, then any tag outside the 22 approved values prefixed "proposed:" as the spec directs. No semantic merging was done — that needs your call.

relationship_type: part_of edges moved onto the child node as part_of; contains edges reversed onto the child; produced_by edges dropped (publisher is a string, not a node); related_to / complements held in _dropped as deferred. Off-union values were poisoning every PageRank score with NaN.
last_updated added as null where absent (required field, string|null).
region filled with the country name where it was null or missing.
releases_per_year: unambiguous single-word cadences resolved to numbers; ambiguous text left in _cadence_original and listed under _gaps.unresolved_cadence.
source_kind mapped to official/commercial; delivered value kept as _source_kind_original.
Non-schema keys Grok wrote (shape, notes, referenced_by, ...) renamed with a leading underscore so they are visibly not part of the schema. Nothing deleted.

domain_semantic_pass.merged_into_existing: Synonyms folded into the 22 already-approved tags (prices→inflation, employment→labour, demography/census→population, monetary/central-bank→monetary-policy, gdp/grdp/regional-accounts→national-accounts, and so on).
domain_semantic_pass.promoted: 17 tags that had earned a slot were promoted out of proposed: and added to Domain in types.ts.
domain_semantic_pass.dropped: Geographic pseudo-tags (regional, provincial, urban, municipal, metropolitan) and batch-meta pseudo-tags (comprehensive, multi-domain, meta, indicators) were removed — geography is already carried by region and jurisdiction_level, and the meta ones describe the batch rather than the report.

_gaps.note: What is genuinely missing and cannot be fixed mechanically — this is the research queue, not a defect list.
